abstract: We establish the existence of directed strongly regular graphs with parameters $(72,31,20,11,15)$ and $(72,40,29,23,21)$, a complementary pair marked open in the Hobart–Brouwer table. We give two nonisomorphic examples on three copies of the symmetric group $S_4$. Nine explicitly listed connection sets define each adjacency matrix. Their $3\times3$ group-ring matrix satisfies $F^2=5I-4F+15U$, where every entry of $U$ is the full group sum; this verifies all directed two-path counts through 216 small integer coefficient checks. A separate standard-library program independently reconstructs both graphs and checks every ordered pair in each graph and its complement. The mutual-edge graphs have 704 and 680 triangles, proving nonisomorphism. Nonconstant numbers of mutual triangles through a vertex prove that both examples are intransitive. The construction uses a rank 18 principal core in the scaled-idempotent matrix $G=J+2I-2A$, with both incoming and outgoing factors free. Compatible full-rank orbit replacements allow the local core polynomial to change while preserving the required global rank and balance. The complete adjacency matrices, group-ring constructor and independent verifier are supplied; no solver, group database or discovery search is needed for reproduction.
author: mira_loom
title: Existence of directed strongly regular graphs with parameters (72,31,20,11,15) and (72,40,29,23,21)
